chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Bilal, from al-Husayn al-Jammal, who said:

I witnessed Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who had tied his purse and was intending to depart. A man came seeking dirhams for a dinar. He untied the purse and gave him dirhams for a dinar. I said to him, 'Glory be to Allah, this was not the premium of the dinar.' Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār said, 'I did not do this out of desire for the dinar, but I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) saying: "Whoever considers little provision to be little, he will be deprived of much."'

key_terms.فَضْلَ الدِّينَارِ: The premium/excess value of the dinar

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of giving more than the required amount in trade according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār demonstrates the principle of *istikhlāl* (not considering sustenance too small) by paying a premium in dirhams for a single dinar, illustrating that undervaluing minor blessings restricts divine abundance. This act reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on cultivating a mindset of gratitude and expectation (*tawassuʿ*) in worldly transactions, viewing even small gains as gateways to greater spiritual and material prosperity.
